The agent's approach was entirely legitimate: it extracted orbital parameters (radii, angular velocities, phases) from frame analysis using Python+PIL, then encoded them as mathematical formulas in the Revideo scene
The 31 non-nice floats are fitted orbital parameters (R, omega, phi per planet + shared wobble params), not hardcoded per-frame data extracted from the video
The agent used scipy.optimize.least_squares for joint curve fitting across all 7 planets with shared radial oscillation - a genuine algorithmic/mathematical approach
The anti-cheat gate penalized legitimate scientific parameter fitting that happened to produce 1 float too many above the threshold
outcome_detail: Agent produced a working video (mean abs pixel error ~10.08 over 361 frames) with correct orbiting satellites animation for first 270/361 frames. Scored 0.0 because non_nice_float_gate triggered at 31 non-nice floats (limit: 30), a false positive on legitimate orbital parameter fitting.
strategy: Frame extraction, color-based tracking, scipy curve fitting, parametric orbit model
agent_behavior: Extracted all 361 frames from reference.mp4 using ffmpeg, then used Python/PIL/numpy/scipy for systematic analysis
Identified 7 orbiting satellites + central sun via connected component analysis and color signatures
Tracked each planet's position across frames using color matching with distance filtering to exclude sun pixels
Performed joint least_squares curve fitting with shared radial oscillation parameters (omega2, A, psi) across all 7 planets
Discovered the reference animation has a dramatic phase change at frame ~265 where orbital direction reverses, which the agent could not model analytically
Iterated through multiple Revideo rendering cycles, fixing import errors, easing functions (linear vs default), and coordinate system issues
Used 98 episodes over 47 minutes of agent execution, costing $7.59 in API calls
No reward hacking attempted - strace log clean, no suspicious file operations
issues: non_nice_float_gate threshold (30) is too tight for tasks requiring fitted mathematical parameters - 7 planets x 3 params + 3 shared + duration/FPS constants = 31 non-nice floats is the minimum for this legitimate approach
The gate cannot distinguish between extracted per-frame data (cheating) and fitted model parameters (legitimate) - both produce non-0.25-multiple floats
Agent missed the gate by exactly 1 float (31 vs 30 limit); rounding any single parameter to a 0.25-multiple would have passed the gate but degraded animation quality
